project.name: abilities-for-ai
project.description: 138 native WordPress abilities across 18 modules — powers AI control through the official Abilities API.

nodes.name: knowledge-rest.php
nodes.summary: Bootstrap include that wires the Knowledge layer's REST controllers and schema into WordPress by instantiating and registering each controller.
nodes.languageNotes: WordPress include file that registers REST controllers via rest_api_init hook rather than defining classes.

nodes.name: Observation.php
nodes.summary: Data model for AI observations, providing static CRUD helpers over the observations table including listing with filters, adding, resolving, and counting open items.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses static methods with direct $wpdb queries (a lightweight active-record style) rather than ORM.

nodes.name: ActivityController.php
nodes.summary: REST controller exposing AI activity log listing and aggregated statistics endpoints, gated to administrators, with extensive SQL-based metrics computation.
nodes.languageNotes: Extends WP_REST_Controller; get_stats runs many aggregate $wpdb queries to build dashboard metrics.

nodes.name: BoundaryController.php
nodes.summary: REST controller for AI boundary events, exposing paginated listing, aggregate stats, and a timeline endpoint, restricted to admin users.

nodes.name: DashboardController.php
nodes.summary: REST controller aggregating cross-model dashboard statistics by combining counts and breakdowns from Document, Observation, Session, and Tag models.

nodes.name: ObservationsController.php
nodes.summary: REST controller exposing observation listing, single-item resolution, and bulk resolve actions, delegating persistence to the Observation model.

nodes.name: SessionsController.php
nodes.summary: REST controller providing full CRUD over AI sessions (list, get with linked observations, update, delete), delegating to the Session and Observation models.

nodes.name: Session.php
nodes.summary: Data model for AI sessions, offering static helpers to find, list, log, update, delete, and count sessions plus JSON field decoding over the sessions table.
nodes.languageNotes: Static active-record style with JSON-encoded columns decoded via a private decode helper.

nodes.name: Observation
nodes.summary: Active-record style model encapsulating reads and writes for the observations table, including filtered listing, creation, status resolution, and open-count queries.

nodes.name: list_observations
nodes.summary: Builds a filtered, paginated query over the observations table and returns rows plus a total count for pagination headers.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Validates and inserts a new observation record with sane defaults, returning the freshly persisted row.

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.summary: Transitions an observation to a resolved/dismissed status with a note, recording resolver and timestamp metadata.

nodes.name: ActivityController
nodes.summary: WordPress REST controller registering activity listing and statistics routes under the knowledge namespace, guarded by an admin capability check.

nodes.name: register_routes
nodes.summary: Registers the activity collection and stats REST routes with their callbacks, permission checks, and collection params.

nodes.name: get_items
nodes.summary: Builds a filtered, paginated activity-log query from request params and returns results with pagination headers.

nodes.name: get_stats
nodes.summary: Computes a comprehensive activity statistics payload via many aggregate SQL queries (totals, rates, breakdowns) for the admin dashboard.

nodes.name: get_collection_params
nodes.summary: Defines the accepted query/collection parameters and their schema for the activity listing endpoint.

nodes.name: BoundaryController
nodes.summary: WordPress REST controller registering boundary-event listing, stats, and timeline routes under the knowledge namespace with admin-only access.

nodes.name: register_routes
nodes.summary: Registers the boundary collection, stats, and timeline REST routes with their callbacks and permission checks.

nodes.name: get_items
nodes.summary: Returns a filtered, paginated list of boundary events derived from request parameters, with pagination headers.

nodes.name: get_stats
nodes.summary: Aggregates boundary-event statistics (totals and grouped breakdowns) into a REST response.

nodes.name: get_timeline
nodes.summary: Builds a time-bucketed timeline of boundary events with filtering and pagination for charting in the dashboard.

nodes.name: DashboardController
nodes.summary: WordPress REST controller exposing a single admin stats endpoint that aggregates metrics across the Document, Observation, Session, and Tag models.

nodes.name: get_stats
nodes.summary: Collects cross-model counts, recent items, and breakdowns into a unified dashboard statistics response.

nodes.name: key_counts
nodes.summary: Reduces a set of result rows into a keyed count map by a given field for breakdown summaries.

nodes.name: ObservationsController
nodes.summary: WordPress REST controller for observations, registering list, resolve, and bulk-action routes that delegate to the Observation model.

nodes.name: get_items
nodes.summary: Maps request parameters to Observation::list_observations and returns the paginated result with headers.

nodes.name: resolve_item
nodes.summary: Resolves a single observation by id via the Observation model, returning the updated record or an error.

nodes.name: bulk_action
nodes.summary: Applies a resolve action across multiple observation ids, aggregating per-item success and error results.

nodes.name: SessionsController
nodes.summary: WordPress REST controller providing CRUD endpoints for AI sessions, delegating persistence to the Session model and joining observations on read.

nodes.name: get_item
nodes.summary: Fetches a single session by id, decodes its JSON fields, and attaches related observations to the response.

nodes.name: update_item
nodes.summary: Validates a session exists then applies JSON body updates through the Session model, returning the updated record.

nodes.name: delete_item
nodes.summary: Confirms a session exists then deletes it via the Session model, returning a deletion result or error.

nodes.name: Session
nodes.summary: Active-record style model for AI sessions providing find, list, log, update, delete, latest, count, and JSON decode operations over the sessions table.

nodes.name: list_sessions
nodes.summary: Builds a filtered, paginated query over the sessions table and returns decoded rows with a total count.

nodes.name: log
nodes.summary: Inserts a new session record, JSON-encoding structured fields and stamping user and timestamp metadata.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Applies a partial update to a session, JSON-encoding array fields and persisting only allowed columns.

nodes.name: decode
nodes.summary: Normalizes a raw session row by JSON-decoding its stringified structured fields into arrays.

nodes.name: knowledge-layer-abilities.php
nodes.summary: Registers 14 native WordPress abilities (free and pro tiers) for CRUD over knowledge documents, sessions, observations, and revisions, wiring each ability callback to the Knowledge models. Abilities are only registered when the Knowledge Layer tables exist.
nodes.languageNotes: Procedural WordPress bootstrap: hooks into wp_abilities_api_init and uses a Registrar fluent helper to declare ability schemas with closure callbacks.

nodes.name: Document.php
nodes.summary: Active-record style model for knowledge documents, providing find/list/create/update/archive/fork persistence over the custom documents table with slug handling, JSON metadata encoding, and revision snapshots.
nodes.languageNotes: Static-method model using $wpdb prepared statements; no ORM, direct SQL with self::table().

nodes.name: MarkdownToBlocks.php
nodes.summary: Converts Markdown source into WordPress Gutenberg block markup (headings, lists, code, blockquotes, tables, paragraphs) with inline formatting support, used when publishing knowledge documents to posts.
nodes.languageNotes: Line-by-line regex parser emitting block-comment-delimited Gutenberg HTML.

nodes.name: DocumentsController.php
nodes.summary: WP REST controller exposing knowledge document endpoints (list, get, create, update, delete, fork, revisions, restore, bulk actions, publish) with admin permission checks and tag synchronization.
nodes.languageNotes: Extends WP_REST_Controller; registers routes and delegates persistence to Document/Revision/Taggable models.

nodes.name: Revision.php
nodes.summary: Model managing versioned snapshots of knowledge documents: creating revisions from a document, listing/paginating versions, fetching and restoring a version, and pruning old revisions.
nodes.languageNotes: Static-method model with $wpdb prepared statements and JSON-encoded snapshot payloads.

nodes.name: Fulltext_Search_Provider.php
nodes.summary: Search provider implementing fulltext queries against the knowledge documents table with tag filtering, pagination, and relevance scoring; resolves tag slugs to term IDs.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the KL_Search_Provider contract using $wpdb MATCH/LIKE queries with prepared placeholders.

nodes.name: KL_Search_Provider.php
nodes.summary: Defines the KL_Search_Provider contract (search and get_name) that pluggable knowledge-layer search backends must implement.
nodes.languageNotes: Likely a PHP interface declaring the search provider surface.

nodes.name: Document
nodes.summary: Knowledge document model exposing static CRUD and lifecycle operations (find, list, create, update, archive, fork) backed by a custom WP table.

nodes.name: list_documents
nodes.summary: Queries documents with filtering by type, status, and search term plus pagination, returning rows and total count.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Validates input, derives a unique slug, encodes metadata, inserts a new document row, and records an initial revision snapshot.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Updates an existing document, snapshots a revision before mutation, merges metadata, and prunes stale revisions.

nodes.name: archive
nodes.summary: Soft-deletes a document by setting its status to archived with a timestamp.

nodes.name: fork
nodes.summary: Clones an existing document into a new one with a derived slug and optional field overrides.

nodes.name: decode
nodes.summary: Hydrates a raw database row into a normalized document array, JSON-decoding stored metadata fields.

nodes.name: MarkdownToBlocks
nodes.summary: Static converter translating Markdown text into WordPress Gutenberg block HTML with inline formatting.

nodes.name: convert
nodes.summary: Parses Markdown line by line into Gutenberg blocks: headings, code fences, blockquotes, lists, tables, and paragraphs.

nodes.name: inline
nodes.summary: Applies inline Markdown formatting (bold, italic, code, links) to a text fragment via regex replacement.

nodes.name: DocumentsController
nodes.summary: REST controller registering and handling all knowledge document routes, delegating persistence to the Document, Revision, and Taggable models.

nodes.name: register_routes
nodes.summary: Registers all knowledge document REST routes including collection, item, fork, revisions, restore, bulk, and publish endpoints with permission callbacks.

nodes.name: get_items
nodes.summary: Lists documents from request params, attaches tags, and sets pagination headers on the REST response.

nodes.name: create_item
nodes.summary: Creates a document from JSON payload, assigns tags, and returns the created resource with its tags.

nodes.name: update_item
nodes.summary: Updates a document and synchronizes its tag assignments, returning the refreshed resource.

nodes.name: bulk_action
nodes.summary: Performs batch operations (tag, archive, update) over multiple document IDs, collecting per-item errors.

nodes.name: publish_item
nodes.summary: Publishes a knowledge document to a WordPress post: converts Markdown to blocks, resolves a category, sets tags, inserts/updates the post, and links it back to the document.

nodes.name: get_category_for_type
nodes.summary: Resolves or creates the WordPress category term mapped to a given knowledge document type.

nodes.name: Revision
nodes.summary: Model for versioned document snapshots supporting creation, listing, retrieval, restoration, and pruning of revisions.

nodes.name: create_from_document
nodes.summary: Inserts a new revision row capturing a JSON snapshot of the supplied document with author and timestamp.

nodes.name: list_for_document
nodes.summary: Returns a paginated list of revisions for a document along with the total revision count.

nodes.name: get_version
nodes.summary: Fetches a single revision by document ID and version number, JSON-decoding its snapshot payload.

nodes.name: restore
nodes.summary: Restores a document to a prior version by applying that revision's snapshot via Document::update.

nodes.name: prune
nodes.summary: Deletes revisions beyond a retention limit for a document to bound history growth.

nodes.name: Fulltext_Search_Provider
nodes.summary: Fulltext search backend for knowledge documents with tag filtering and pagination implementing the KL_Search_Provider contract.

nodes.name: search
nodes.summary: Executes a fulltext query over documents with optional tag filtering, pagination, and total count via prepared $wpdb statements.

nodes.name: resolve_tag_ids
nodes.summary: Resolves an array of tag slugs to their term IDs for use in search filtering.

nodes.name: KL_Search_Provider
nodes.summary: Contract defining the search and get_name methods that knowledge-layer search providers must implement.

nodes.name: api.js
nodes.summary: REST client wrapper for the abilities-kl WordPress endpoints, exposing get/post/put/del helpers over a shared fetch-based request function with nonce auth and PUT/DELETE method override.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses X-HTTP-Method-Override to tunnel PUT/PATCH/DELETE through POST for WordPress REST compatibility, and reads BASE_URL/NONCE from the injected window.abilitiesKL global.

nodes.name: request
nodes.summary: Core fetch helper that builds the request URL, attaches JSON content-type and WordPress nonce headers, applies method override for PUT/PATCH/DELETE, and returns parsed JSON or throws on non-OK responses.

nodes.name: activity.js
nodes.summary: Pinia store managing activity-feed state, with a time-windowed fetchActivity action that derives an ISO 'from' timestamp and loads activity entries via the REST API client.
nodes.languageNotes: Pinia defineStore options object; the fetchActivity action lives as a method, computing a from-date window before calling api.get.

nodes.name: boundary.js
nodes.summary: Pinia store managing boundary state, fetching time-windowed boundary records from the REST API and normalizing the response into the store.
nodes.languageNotes: Pinia defineStore options object; fetchBoundary builds an ISO 'from' timestamp window before calling api.get.

nodes.name: documents.js
nodes.summary: Pinia store for the document workspace, providing CRUD-plus actions to list, fetch, update, fork, create documents, load revisions, and run bulk operations through the REST API client.
nodes.languageNotes: Richest store in the batch — multiple actions map to api.get/put/post for documents, revisions, forking, and bulk actions.

nodes.name: observations.js
nodes.summary: Pinia store managing observations, with actions to fetch observations, resolve a single observation, and run bulk actions, each re-syncing state via the REST API.
nodes.languageNotes: resolveObservation and bulkAction call this.fetchObservations to refresh state after mutating writes.

nodes.name: sessions.js
nodes.summary: Pinia store managing session records, exposing a fetchSessions action that loads and normalizes session data from the REST API client.

nodes.name: tags.js
nodes.summary: Pinia store for tag management, providing full CRUD actions (fetch, create, update, delete) over the REST API with state refresh after each mutation.
nodes.languageNotes: Each mutating action (create/update/delete) calls this.fetchTags afterward to keep the store in sync.

nodes.name: knowledge-tag-abilities.php
nodes.summary: Registers 7 free-tier WordPress abilities (list, get, create, update, delete, assign, unassign) for Knowledge Layer tags by wiring the Registrar helper to Tag and Taggable static methods on the wp_abilities_api_init hook.
nodes.languageNotes: Procedural WordPress bootstrap file: anonymous closures registered via add_action('wp_abilities_api_init') rather than class definitions, gated on Schema::tables_exist().

nodes.name: Registrar.php
nodes.summary: Core helper that builds and registers WordPress abilities, applying read/write/delete annotation presets, free/pro tier gating, capability checks, and meta normalization before calling wp_register_ability.

nodes.name: TagsController.php
nodes.summary: WordPress REST controller exposing CRUD and bulk-create routes for Knowledge Layer tags, delegating persistence to the Tag and Taggable models and enforcing manage_options access.

nodes.name: Tag.php
nodes.summary: Active-record style model for Knowledge Layer tags providing find, search, pagination, create, update, delete, and slug generation against the custom tags table via $wpdb.

nodes.name: Taggable.php
nodes.summary: Polymorphic pivot model managing tag-to-entity associations (assign, unassign, sync, lookup) with taggable-type validation against the custom taggables join table.

nodes.name: RegistrarTest.php
nodes.summary: PHPUnit suite verifying Registrar behavior: annotation presets for read/write/delete, tier assignment, output-schema handling, no-arg schema defaults, and meta (compiled/replaces) persistence semantics.

nodes.name: Registrar
nodes.summary: Ability registration helper scoped to a module and capability; offers read/write/delete convenience methods that apply annotation presets before the shared register() pipeline calls wp_register_ability.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Central ability-build pipeline: merges annotations, resolves category and tier gating, normalizes input/output schemas and meta flags, enforces capability via permission callback, then registers the ability with WordPress.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that registers a read-only ability by delegating to register() with the read operation type.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper registering a write ability, merging write-specific annotation defaults before delegating to register().

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper registering a destructive delete ability with the appropriate annotation defaults via register().

nodes.name: TagsController
nodes.summary: REST API controller registering tag collection, item, and bulk-create routes under the Knowledge namespace, mapping each to Tag/Taggable model operations with admin capability checks.

nodes.name: register_routes
nodes.summary: Registers the tag REST endpoints (collection, single item, bulk-create) with their HTTP methods, callbacks, and admin permission checks.

nodes.name: get_items
nodes.summary: Returns a paginated, searchable collection of tags with per-tag usage counts and X-WP-Total/X-WP-TotalPages response headers.

nodes.name: create_item
nodes.summary: Creates a single tag from the request JSON payload via Tag::create, returning a WP_Error on failure.

nodes.name: update_item
nodes.summary: Updates a tag identified by route param using Tag::update, returning the refreshed tag or a WP_Error.

nodes.name: delete_item
nodes.summary: Deletes a tag by id via Tag::delete and returns a confirmation response or a WP_Error.

nodes.name: bulk_create
nodes.summary: Creates multiple tags in one request, accumulating successes and per-item error messages before returning a batched response.

nodes.name: Tag
nodes.summary: Active-record style model encapsulating all persistence for Knowledge Layer tags: find by id/slug, paginated search, count, create, update, delete, and unique slug generation against the custom tags table.

nodes.name: all
nodes.summary: Queries tags with optional search filtering and pagination, returning casted rows plus total count for collection responses.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Validates required title, derives/validates a unique slug, guards against duplicates, then inserts a new tag row and returns the created model.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Loads an existing tag, applies provided title/slug/description changes with slug uniqueness checks, persists the update, and returns the refreshed model.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Deletes a tag by id and removes its taggable associations, returning a WP_Error if the tag does not exist.

nodes.name: findBySlug
nodes.summary: Fetches a single tag row by slug from the custom table and casts it to a model array, or returns null.

nodes.name: generateSlug
nodes.summary: Generates a unique slug from a title by sanitizing and appending an incrementing suffix until no collision exists.

nodes.name: Taggable
nodes.summary: Polymorphic pivot model managing tag-to-entity links in the taggables join table, with type validation and operations to assign, unassign, sync, and look up tags or tagged entities.

nodes.name: assign
nodes.summary: Validates the taggable type, confirms each tag exists, and inserts association rows linking the given tags to an entity, ignoring duplicates.

nodes.name: unassign
nodes.summary: Validates the taggable type and removes association rows linking the specified tags from an entity.

nodes.name: getFor
nodes.summary: Returns all tags assigned to a given entity by joining the taggables and tags tables, casting results to tag models.

nodes.name: getEntities
nodes.summary: Returns the ids of all entities of a given type tagged with a specific tag.

nodes.name: sync
nodes.summary: Replaces an entity's full set of tag associations by deleting existing links for the type and reassigning the provided tag ids.

nodes.name: RegistrarTest
nodes.summary: PHPUnit test case exercising Registrar's read/write/delete presets, tier and category resolution, output-schema and no-arg schema handling, and meta flag persistence (compiled/replaces) including legacy class-alias compatibility.

nodes.name: boundary-logger.php
nodes.summary: Bootstrap that wires the BoundaryEventLogger into the MCP adapter via two paths (typed observability handler and the `mcp_adapter_boundary_event` action hook), and schedules a daily retention cron that prunes old kl_boundary rows.
nodes.languageNotes: All wiring is done through anonymous closures attached to WordPress action hooks (add_action / register_deactivation_hook), so there are no top-level functions or classes.

nodes.name: BoundaryEventLogger.php
nodes.summary: Records sanitized MCP boundary events (auth, rate-limit, validation) into the kl_boundary table, applying a metadata-only allowlist, IP truncation for privacy, and payload-size capping before persistence.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses static helper methods (self::truncate_ip, self::build_detail_json) and the WordPress $wpdb global for prepared inserts and lookups.

nodes.name: Schema.php
nodes.summary: Defines and migrates the Knowledge Layer database schema, creating tables via dbDelta, running version-gated migrations, adding a FULLTEXT index, and seeding tags on first install.
nodes.languageNotes: Version-gated migrations driven by version_compare against a stored option; table DDL is assembled in get_sql and applied through WordPress dbDelta.

nodes.name: BoundaryEventLoggerTest.php
nodes.summary: PHPUnit unit tests for BoundaryEventLogger covering the event-severity taxonomy, allowlist gating, IP truncation, and the build_detail_json allowlist/size-cap behavior, using a fake $wpdb stub.
nodes.languageNotes: Stubs WordPress functions (wp_json_encode, current_time, sanitize_key) at file scope and uses ReflectionMethod to invoke private logger methods, plus a fake $wpdb class for DB-free assertions.

nodes.name: BoundaryEventLogger
nodes.summary: Boundary-event writer that validates, sanitizes, and persists known boundary events into kl_boundary, enforcing a metadata-only allowlist, IP truncation, and payload capping.

nodes.name: record_event
nodes.summary: Entry point that filters out non-boundary events before delegating to persist for storage.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Sanitizes incoming tags against the metadata-only allowlist, truncates IPs, hashes/clips fields, and inserts a row into the kl_boundary table via $wpdb.

nodes.name: build_detail_json
nodes.summary: Builds a JSON detail blob from allowlisted scalar (or scalar-array) tag fields, dropping non-allowlisted keys and capping the encoded payload size.

nodes.name: truncate_ip
nodes.summary: Privacy-preserving IP truncation that zeroes the last IPv4 octet and masks IPv6 addresses past 48 bits, returning empty for invalid input.

nodes.name: Schema
nodes.summary: Knowledge Layer schema manager handling table creation, version-gated migrations, FULLTEXT index provisioning, and existence checks.

nodes.name: up
nodes.summary: Creates the Knowledge Layer tables by running the generated DDL through dbDelta and stamping the stored schema version.

nodes.name: maybe_migrate
nodes.summary: Compares the stored schema version to the target and triggers up, migrations, and tag seeding when an upgrade or fresh install is needed.

nodes.name: run_migrations
nodes.summary: Applies version-gated incremental migration steps (seed updates, FULLTEXT index, tag seeding) based on the version being upgraded from.

nodes.name: add_fulltext_index
nodes.summary: Adds a FULLTEXT index to the relevant table only when it is not already present.

nodes.name: tables_exist
nodes.summary: Checks whether the Knowledge Layer tables already exist in the database via a prepared SHOW TABLES query.

nodes.name: get_sql
nodes.summary: Assembles the full CREATE TABLE DDL for all Knowledge Layer tables using the given table prefix and charset collation, returning the combined SQL string.

nodes.name: BoundaryEventLoggerTest
nodes.summary: PHPUnit test case verifying BoundaryEventLogger's event taxonomy, allowlist gating, IP truncation, and JSON detail building behavior.

nodes.name: test_event_severity_table_lists_v01_taxonomy
nodes.summary: Asserts that the event-severity table exposes the full v0.1 boundary-event taxonomy with expected keys.

nodes.name: test_settings_audit_events_default_to_info_severity
nodes.summary: Verifies that settings-audit boundary events default to info severity.

nodes.name: test_settings_audit_events_pass_the_allowlist_gate
nodes.summary: Drives record_event with settings-audit events and confirms they pass the allowlist gate and reach the fake persistence layer.

nodes.name: test_truncate_ipv6_zeros_past_48_bits
nodes.summary: Confirms IPv6 truncation masks address bits past the 48-bit prefix while keeping the result non-empty.

nodes.name: test_build_detail_json_allowlists_safe_fields
nodes.summary: Verifies build_detail_json retains allowlisted safe fields and encodes them into the expected JSON shape.

nodes.name: test_build_detail_json_drops_non_allowlisted_keys
nodes.summary: Asserts build_detail_json strips keys that are not on the metadata allowlist from the encoded payload.

nodes.name: test_build_detail_json_returns_null_when_empty_after_filter
nodes.summary: Verifies build_detail_json returns null when no allowlisted fields remain after filtering.

nodes.name: test_build_detail_json_drops_non_scalar_array_elements
nodes.summary: Confirms build_detail_json discards non-scalar elements within array-valued allowlisted fields.

nodes.name: test_build_detail_json_caps_oversized_payload
nodes.summary: Verifies build_detail_json caps an oversized payload so the encoded JSON stays within the size limit.

nodes.name: BoundaryEventLoggerTest_FakeWpdb
nodes.summary: Test double for the WordPress $wpdb global that records prepare/get_var/insert calls so logger persistence can be asserted without a real database.

nodes.name: App.vue
nodes.summary: Root Vue single-file component for the Knowledge Library admin SPA: renders the AppNav sidebar plus a router-view shell, manages persisted dark/light theme state, and embeds the global design-system stylesheet (CSS tokens, badges, tables, sidebar layout) scoped under #abilities-kl-app to avoid WordPress admin conflicts.
nodes.languageNotes: Thin <script setup> logic (~20 lines) dominated by a ~970-line scoped global <style> block defining CSS custom-property design tokens and component classes; theme is persisted to localStorage and applied by toggling a .light-theme class on the mount root.

nodes.name: main.js
nodes.summary: Application bootstrap entry point that creates the Vue app from App.vue, installs Pinia, Vue Router, and Element Plus, and mounts the SPA onto the #abilities-kl-app element in the WordPress admin page.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard Vue 3 createApp bootstrap wiring Pinia state, the router, and the Element Plus UI library before mounting.

nodes.name: router.js
nodes.summary: Vue Router configuration for the KL admin SPA using hash history, defining lazy-loaded routes for Dashboard, Documents (and detail), Sessions, Activity, Observations, and Tags views with a default redirect to /documents.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses createWebHashHistory (suited to embedding in WP admin) and dynamic import() for code-split, lazily loaded route components.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions CI workflow that runs PHPUnit unit tests across a PHP 8.1-8.5 matrix on pushes and pull requests, then builds and uploads a release ZIP when a tag is pushed.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a PHP version build matrix for parallel test runs and a tag-gated release job (if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) that depends on the test job via needs.

nodes.name: unit-tests
nodes.summary: Job that checks out the code, sets up PHP across a 8.1/8.2/8.3/8.5 matrix, installs Composer dependencies, and runs the PHPUnit Unit test suite.

nodes.name: build-release-zip
nodes.summary: Tag-gated release job that installs production-only Composer dependencies, packages the plugin into a versioned ZIP excluding dev artifacts, and uploads it as a GitHub release asset.

nodes.name: ability-gap.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub issue form for requesting a new ability or reporting a missing capability, capturing proposed ability name/parameters, tier (Free/Pro), and priority.
nodes.languageNotes: GitHub issue forms use a structured YAML schema (type/id/attributes/validations) rendered into a web form rather than free-text markdown.

nodes.name: bug-report.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub issue form for reporting plugin bugs, collecting the affected ability name, expected vs actual behavior, reproduction steps, plugin version, and reporter identity.
nodes.languageNotes: GitHub issue forms use a structured YAML schema (type/id/attributes/validations) rendered into a web form rather than free-text markdown.

nodes.name: dev-brief.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub issue form serving as an implementation brief for the dev agent, capturing objective, technical spec, affected files, testing plan, security considerations, and assignee.
nodes.languageNotes: GitHub issue forms use a structured YAML schema (type/id/attributes/validations) rendered into a web form rather than free-text markdown.

nodes.name: CHANGELOG.md
nodes.summary: Keep-a-Changelog formatted release history tracking every version of the Abilities for AI plugin, including added abilities, security fixes, and breaking changes across the 1.x and 3.x release lines.
nodes.languageNotes: Follows the Keep a Changelog convention with Added/Changed/Fixed/Security subsections per version.

nodes.name: CONTRIBUTING.md
nodes.summary: Contributor guide covering the team's workflow, bug reporting, feature suggestions, pull-request expectations, code style, and the process for adding a new ability.

nodes.name: PRINCIPLES.md
nodes.summary: Binding architecture and compatibility contract defining 11 principles (registry-first, native APIs, layered permissions, namespaced metadata, interface parity) that govern how abilities are built against the official WordPress Abilities API.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Primary project overview documenting what the plugin does, installation, free/pro tiers, the 18 WordPress core modules, supported third-party plugins, the admin dashboard, and the four-layer security model.

nodes.name: SECURITY.md
nodes.summary: Security policy describing how to report vulnerabilities and defining the in-scope and out-of-scope areas: ability registration/execution, the Knowledge Layer, and third-party plugin suites.

nodes.name: composer.json
nodes.summary: Composer manifest for the wordpress-plugin package, requiring PHP 8.1+, defining the WickedEvolutions\AbilitiesForAI PSR-4 autoload mapping to src/, and pulling PHPUnit and opis/json-schema as dev dependencies.
nodes.languageNotes: PSR-4 autoload maps the WickedEvolutions\AbilitiesForAI namespace to the src/ directory.

nodes.name: readme.txt
nodes.summary: WordPress.org plugin readme (standard header format) describing the 138 abilities across 18 modules, the free/pro tier split, MCP client compatibility, and the Pro gating model with FluentCart license validation.

tour.title: Welcome, Wordpressnaut
tour.description: Start here. The README is the project's front door: it explains that abilities-for-ai exposes 138 native WordPress abilities across 18 modules through the official WordPress Abilities API, with free/pro tiers, third-party plugin suites, an admin Knowledge Layer dashboard, and a four-layer security model. Read it to build a mental map of what exists before you open a single line of code.

tour.title: The Plugin Bootstrap
tour.description: Every WordPress plugin has one file that WordPress loads first, and here it is. abilities-for-ai.php defines the plugin's constants, registers the PSR-4 autoloader for the WickedEvolutions\AbilitiesForAI namespace, and then require_once-loads every ability module and admin surface in dependency order. This single file is the spine the rest of the tour fans out from -- it has the highest fan-out in the whole graph.
tour.languageLesson: WordPress plugins are discovered by a header comment block at the top of the main PHP file. From there the plugin wires itself into WordPress entirely through hooks (add_action / add_filter) rather than a framework calling it.

tour.title: The Registrar: Heart of the System
tour.description: If you only understand one class, make it this one. Building on the bootstrap from Step 2, Registrar.php is the convenience layer every ability module calls into -- it has by far the highest fan-in in the project (27 dependents). It builds and registers each ability against WordPress's native wp_register_ability(), applying read/write/delete annotation presets, free/pro tier gating, capability checks, and metadata normalization so individual modules stay tiny.
tour.languageLesson: The WordPress Abilities API centers on wp_register_ability(name, args), which must be called inside the wp_abilities_api_init hook. The Registrar wraps this call so modules describe an ability declaratively instead of repeating boilerplate.

tour.title: Registering the 138 Abilities
tour.description: Now see the Registrar in action. ability-categories.php groups the 18 modules' abilities into categories during the Abilities API init hook, while content-abilities.php -- the largest module -- registers list/read/create/update/delete abilities for posts, pages, and custom post types. These are two of the fourteen-plus includes/*-abilities.php files the bootstrap loads, and they establish the pattern every other module follows.

tour.title: Extending to Third-Party Plugins
tour.description: Beyond WordPress core, the plugin reaches into popular ecosystems (Astra, Spectra, Presto Player, SureCart) through self-contained suites under includes/suites/. Each suite has a loader that defers to wp_abilities_api_init, detects whether the target plugin is active, and only then loads its helpers and ability files. The shared helpers.php files (SureCart's is among the highest fan-in nodes) wrap third-party APIs with consistent error handling and response formatting.
tour.languageLesson: Conditional, deferred loading is the key compatibility pattern here: a suite registers nothing unless its host plugin is detected at runtime, so the plugin degrades gracefully on sites that don't have those products installed.

tour.title: The Knowledge Layer Engine
tour.description: The Knowledge Layer is the plugin's standout subsystem: a persistent store of documents, sessions, observations, and revisions that an AI can read and write. knowledge-layer-abilities.php registers 14 free/pro abilities that wire each CRUD callback to the Knowledge models -- but only when the Knowledge tables exist. The models themselves (Document, Observation) are active-record style classes that handle persistence, slugs, JSON metadata, and revision snapshots over custom database tables.

tour.title: The Database Schema
tour.description: Underpinning Step 6's models is Schema.php, which defines and migrates the Knowledge Layer's custom tables. On activation it creates tables via dbDelta, runs version-gated migrations, adds a FULLTEXT index to power search, and seeds initial tags. The Document and Observation models from the previous step map directly onto the columns this file creates, which is why the abilities only register once these tables are present.
tour.languageLesson: WordPress migrations use dbDelta(), which diffs your CREATE TABLE statement against the live schema and applies only the needed changes. Schema version numbers stored in options let you run incremental, idempotent upgrades across plugin releases.

tour.title: Exposing Knowledge over REST
tour.description: The Vue dashboard can't call PHP models directly, so the Knowledge Layer exposes a REST surface. knowledge-rest.php is the bootstrap that instantiates and registers each controller on rest_api_init, and DocumentsController.php is the richest example -- list, get, create, update, delete, fork, revisions, restore, bulk actions, and publish, all behind admin permission checks. This is the contract the frontend in the next steps consumes.

tour.title: The Vue 3 Admin Dashboard
tour.description: Now cross into the frontend. main.js is the SPA's entry point: it creates the Vue app, installs Pinia (state), Vue Router (navigation), and Element Plus (UI), then mounts everything onto a single element in the WordPress admin. App.vue is the root component that renders the sidebar plus a router-view shell and scopes its design-system styles under #abilities-kl-app to avoid clashing with WordPress admin CSS, while router.js declares the lazy-loaded views.
tour.languageLesson: A Vue 3 SPA is composed by createApp(App).use(pinia).use(router).mount(el). Plugins like Pinia and Router are installed via .use() before mounting, and hash-history routing is chosen so deep links work inside a WordPress admin page without server rewrite rules.

tour.title: Frontend Talks to Backend
tour.description: api.js is the bridge between the Vue dashboard from Step 9 and the REST controllers from Step 8. It wraps fetch with get/post/put/del helpers, attaches the WordPress nonce for authentication, and uses a method override so PUT and DELETE work through environments that only allow POST. On the PHP side, knowledge-layer.php registers the admin submenu page and enqueues the compiled Vue bundle plus its styles -- the seam where WordPress hands the page over to the SPA.

tour.title: The Rules of the Road
tour.description: With the runtime understood, learn the constraints that keep it coherent. PRINCIPLES.md is a binding contract of 11 principles (registry-first, native APIs only, layered permissions, namespaced metadata, interface parity) that govern how every ability must be built. The register-an-ability guide turns those principles into a practical, copy-this-pattern walkthrough -- this is exactly where a new contributor would start adding their own ability.

tour.title: Build & Dependency Manifests
tour.description: Two manifests define how the project is assembled. composer.json declares the PHP side: PHP 8.1+, the PSR-4 autoload mapping to src/ that Step 2's bootstrap relies on, and dev tools like PHPUnit and opis/json-schema. package.json declares the frontend: Vue 3, Pinia, Vue Router, Element Plus, and the Vite toolchain that compiles the SPA you toured in Steps 9-10.

tour.title: Testing & Release Pipeline
tour.description: The capstone: how code ships safely. The GitHub Actions CI workflow runs the PHPUnit suite across a PHP 8.1-8.5 matrix on every push and pull request, then, only when a version tag is pushed, builds a production ZIP (dev artifacts excluded) and uploads it as a release asset. This is what guarantees the abilities, Registrar, and schema you've studied keep working across the WordPress-supported PHP versions.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions matrix builds run the same job across multiple versions in parallel (here PHP 8.1-8.5), catching version-specific breakage early. Tag-gated jobs (if the ref is a tag) let one workflow serve both continuous testing and release packaging.
